svg.title: Past search schematic 07: Kh. Qumran: where searchers dug for the scroll's deposits, and what else was excavated
svg.text: Past searches 07 — Kh. Qumran: where searchers dug for the scroll's deposits, and what else was excavated
Schematic plan, north up, NOT to scale: positions are rough, after published plans; only the sources' own distances and depths are given.
Site plan (schematic)
Blue = dug, cleared or reached (who, when); dashed with ? = footprint or position not given.
Ochre dashed = measured only. Grey = no digging recorded. Red = Allegro's scroll item there.
main
building
tower
large hall
aqueduct from the W: rock-cut in the Wadi Qumran
gorge, then built across the marl plateau for
upwards of 400 yards (Masterman, QS 1903)
2002: route mapped by total station (Reeder
and Jol 2006). Measured only, not dug.
Allegro's item 21 (entry 20): the dam (?)
in the Valley of Secacah, buried 1 cubit. He takes
the valley as the Wadi Qumran gorge (1960 Fig. 2).
No fieldwork. Magen and Peleg surmise a dam in
the upper gorge, “no remains of which survived”
Allegro's item 22 (entry 21): head of the
conduit at the settling basin, NW (1960 Fig. 4;
dropped 1964).
No fieldwork reported.
2009: probe along a wall near the L138 bath
(Peleg's IAA licence; Barfield's group watched).
To “virgin rock”; area not given. Blogs only (S17).
L120 (diamond): three silver hoards, 561
coins (de Vaux 1955; ledger S02).
1959–60, Allegro (S28): an animal-bone pot deposit
“hidden inside an interior wall”, found by a
detector near the hoard (1964 pp. 68–69).
Room not named.
Magen and Peleg: an early channel under the floors
of L115/L116, by the round cistern L110 (2018 p. 82).
Large hall: Allegro's “Hall of Congregation”.
Its locus number is not given in the repo.
1959–60, Allegro (S03): after a detector reading,
a “narrow trench” at the W end of the hall (1964;
“one end”, 1966): pottery, animal bones and an
oven under the plaster floor. No depth or item no.
1959–60, Allegro (S28): “one very shallow trench
outside the main group of buildings”, in an
open courtyard “at a point indicated by the
scroll” (1964 pp. 67–68). No result stated. Position
not given: the box is a placeholder.
Allegro's item 24 (entry 23), probably (repo
inference): 60 cubits from the “Solomon” aqueduct
toward the watchtower, buried 3 cubits (1964). In
1960 he put the spot midway along the S wall of the
great courtyard (Fig. 4).

Magen and Peleg 1993–2004 (S18): the N
dump, c. 10 m N of the site, and a smaller NW
De Vaux had partly dug the N dump (“Section A”,
2007 n. 8). Areas and depths not compiled.
R. de Vaux, seasons 1953–56 (S02): the buildings
excavated (pale blue); L138 is in his 1955
journal. Extent and depths not compiled.
The great cistern on the E side, split lengthwise
by the crack (dashed); one side “dropped some
two feet”. 1959–60 (S28): Allegro's party crawled
into the gap under the plaster: “a few pieces of
broken pottery” (1964 p. 65). No locus in the repo.
Allegro's item 23 (entry 22): the fissure in the
“Solomon” reservoir; tithe vessels (1960, 1964).
De Vaux 1953 p. 312: damage crosses two
interior pools N–S, the east side sunk.
main cemetery on the

over a thousand
(Masterman 1902); c. 1,100
(Allegro 1964)
1874: one grave opened
(QS 1874): no objects; a
brick over the body at
Bodies c. 4½ ft down in side niches (excavators,
via Allegro 1964 pp. 69–70).
1912: some graves newly disturbed, perhaps by
treasure hunters (Masterman, QS 1913 p. 43).
Allegro's item 25 (entry 24): a tomb in the
Wadi Kippa, on the way from Jericho, 7 cubits
No such tomb known to him; not located; not dug.
Who did what, when
Fieldwork at the site itself that the repo's sources report.
Drake and Clermont-Ganneau open one grave;
no objects (QS 1874 pp. 74, 83).
Masterman sees at least three graves lying
open; measures a stepped birket 67 × 16⅔
ft, 10 ft deep (QS 1902 pp. 161–162).
De Vaux excavates the buildings, finding
the L120 hoards (seasons as in S02; his
first-season report is RB 60, 1953).
Allegro: detectors and the hall trench
(S03); the crawl, the courtyard trench and
the wall deposit (S28, 1964 book only).
Allegro: “winter 1959-60”; Wright: April
1960 at Mird.
Magen and Peleg (S18): renewed excavation,
dumps and under some floors.
A probe near L138 for J. Barfield, to
bedrock (S17; CLAIM grade).
No depth recorded
Allegro's hall trench (S03); his “very shallow”
courtyard trench and the gap he crawled into (S28).
De Vaux and Magen and Peleg: not compiled in the repo.
Allegro: the excavations “usually stopped at the lower
floor levels” (1964 p. 160).
The 2009 probe: “virgin rock”, no figure.
Depths that are given: the 1960 detectors' reach, c. 18
Allegro's three books differ
1960: no fieldwork; Fig. 4 marks items 22–24 on de
Vaux's plan.
1964: four actions at Qumran; Fig. 6 drops the item 22
and 24 marks and shows no trench.
1966: only the hall trench (at “one end”); no item.
Scroll entries
Atlas: Kh. Qumran is the preferred candidate for entries
21 and 22, a possible one for 20, 23, 25 and 26. Allegro's
item numbers are his own; tables/entry_concordance.csv
matches his items 21–25 to entries 20–24: same lines and
same passages, checked against his text.
Sources
Allegro, Treasure of the Copper Scroll (1960) pp. 70–74, Figs. 2, 4; 2nd ed. (1964) pp. 63–70, 160;
Search in the Desert (1966) pp. 92–94. Ledger rows S02, S03, S17, S18, S28. Humbert and Chambon 2016
table); Reeder and Jol 2006; tables/entry_concordance.csv.
How it was drawn
Schematic, after the plans of de Vaux (Strobel 1972 Fig. 1) and Magen and Peleg 2018 Fig. 9; rough
positions only. The hall is drawn as the long room S of the main building (inference).
What it shows
In 1959–60 Allegro's party worked at four spots (S03, S28); none has a depth, and two have no stated
position. The only other dig for a deposit, the 2009 probe near L138, is known only from blogs. De
Vaux's and Magen and Peleg's excavations are not compiled by area or depth.
What it does not show
Whether any deposit is or is not here: no search has a stated target volume and depth. The caves near
the site (sheet 01) and the gorge intake are not drawn.
